title: Political Science
description: ISC Class XI Political Science: the Constitution and political theory.

syllabusBaselines.source: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2027 Regulations and Syllabuses - Political Science (subject code 852) (www.cisce.org).
syllabusBaselines.note: Verified October 2026 against the CISCE-copyrighted ISC Year 2027 Political Science (852) syllabus document with a CLASS XI section, read through its AglaSem reproduction because cisce.org returns 403 to automated fetches, with a Scribd copy as corroboration. Class XI prescribes Paper I Theory (3 hours, 80 marks) in Section A Political Theory and Section B Contemporary International Relations, and Paper II Project Work (20 marks); all twelve units are registered below.

sections.title: Political Science (Paper I)
sections.paperLabel: ISC Class XI · Paper I · Theory (80 marks)
sections.description: Section A: Political Theory (eight units). Section B: Contemporary International Relations (four units). Paper II carries project work of 20 marks.

chapters.title: Introduction to Political Science and State
chapters.blurb: The meaning and scope of political science and its branches, the elements of the State — population, territory, government and sovereignty — and the State distinguished from the Nation.

chapters.title: The Origin of the State
chapters.blurb: Theories of the origin of the State: the divine origin theory and the social contract theories of Hobbes, Locke and Rousseau, examined for their features.

chapters.title: Political Ideologies
chapters.blurb: Liberalism and communism: their meanings and defining features, from individual rights and democracy to dialectical materialism and the classless society.

chapters.title: Sovereignty
chapters.blurb: The meaning, kinds and characteristics of sovereignty, with a historical analysis, Austin's theory and the pluralist view.

chapters.title: Law
chapters.blurb: The meaning of law, its sources — customs, usages, religion, judicial decisions, scientific commentaries, equity and legislation — and its kinds from municipal to international law.

chapters.title: Liberty
chapters.blurb: Liberty: its meaning, its negative and positive dimensions, and its civil, political and economic kinds.

chapters.title: Equality
chapters.blurb: Equality: its meaning and its legal, social, political and economic kinds.

chapters.title: Justice
chapters.blurb: The meaning of justice and the contemporary theories of John Rawls and Amartya Sen, examined for their features.

chapters.title: Disintegration of the Soviet Union
chapters.blurb: The causes of the disintegration of the Soviet Union — political and economic stagnation, Gorbachev's reforms and rising nationalism — and its impact: the end of the cold war and the emergence of new states.

chapters.title: Unipolar World
chapters.blurb: U.S. unilateralism in a unipolar world, with case studies of Iraq and Afghanistan, and India's defence and trade relations with the USA after 1991.

chapters.title: Regional Cooperation
chapters.blurb: Regional cooperation through ASEAN, the European Union, SAARC, BRICS and QUAD — their aims and economic achievements.

chapters.title: South Asia
chapters.blurb: India's relationships with its neighbours: Pakistan from the 1965 war to Kargil, Bangladesh over water and migration, and China from Panchsheel to the 1962 war.
